MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit, will not be reviewed beyond page 2 or may be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ 1. Executive Leadership in Integrated Industrial Environments: Demonstrated experience leading large-scale industrial production and engineering organizations (specifically equivalent to Naval Shipyard Codes 200, 300, 700, and/or 900) with proven ability to integrate technical authority/engineering planning with waterfront industrial execution to achieve mission outcomes. TQ 2. Strategic Change Management: Demonstrated success in organization strategic plan development and organizational transformation, such as consolidating departments or implementing Lean/Theory of Constraints (TOC) methodologies. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Director for Production Operations for Norfolk Naval Shipyard (NNSY) and be located at NNSY headquarters, in Portsmouth, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will exercise comprehensive executive authority and strategic leadership across the enterprise, driving program management, resource allocation, and policy execution to meet critical national security missions.

You will coordinate, communicate, and make decisions with internal and external stakeholders while liaising with stakeholders to build a seamless and integrated workforce development and product delivery plan.

You will establish production priorities, allocate trade resources and set performance standards to drive Production Resources to ensure disciplined, high-quality work packages across submarine, aircraft carrier and surface ship maintenance programs.
You will integrate project management, facilities, and dry dock operations to guarantee Fleet delivery schedules.
You will lead, mentor, and develop a massive, highly diverse workforce comprising professional engineers, project managers, and skilled industrial tradespeople.
You will directly manage department heads for the Operations department, Production Resources department, aircraft carrier and submarine program offices and Lifting and Handling department.
You will actively champion human capital development, workforce development, team building and process improvement while enforcing Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) standards.
You will act as the executive authority on the waterfront, directly interfacing with Fleet and Type Commander leadership to synchronize delivery schedules and resolve high-level technical challenges.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as Director for Supply Chain Performance and Integration, Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) lead expert in supply chain policy and performance. Authoritative expert and advisor to COMNAVSUP on Navy supply chain performance, technology employment, and systems integration. Provides senior leadership and oversight to subordinate commands, including Weapon Systems Support and regional FLCs.

You will set the enterprise supply chain vision and management philosophy for NAVSUP, continuously assess strategies, goals, and performance; redirect efforts and resources to ensure alignment with Navy objectives and the Commander's intent.

You will serve as the enterprise focal point for NAVSUP supply chain accountability and visibility. Maintain an enterprise-wide program supporting the Commander to ensure compliance with all DoW and DON requirements in this critical area.
You will direct formulation of policies, plans and procedures to evaluate execution of the command's supply chain performance.
You will represent NAVSUP's supply chain management and related services interests at the office of CNO, SECNAV and SECWAR as required as the lead in Navy ERP Program.

You will provide policy and direction for spending over $30B across the FYDP on spares and repairs for aviation, surface, and subsurface readiness. Hold oversight responsibility for a $32B Navy material inventory.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The National Guard Bureau serves as a joint activity of the Department of War (under both the Department of the Army and Department of the Air Force). Its primary purposes are: To act as the official channel of communication between the Department of War and the 54 states, territories, and the District of Columbia (the "54"). To ensure the Army National Guard and Air National Guard are properly organized, manned, trained, equipped, and resourced to perform their federal and state missions. To administer federal policies, programs, and resources for the National Guard.
MajorDuties: The Inspector General is the Department of War Component Inspector General for the NGB and serves as the principal advisor to the CNGB (O-10) and the Vice CNGB (O-10) on all assessed matters relating to the discipline, efficiency, economy, morale, training, and readiness of the NG and NGB, and other oversight matters of importance. NGB-IG as a Personal Staff officer to CNGB serves as an information conduit, with advice on strategic issues and general officer matters within the National Guard. The incumbent liaises with persons and organizations outside NGB to include collaboration with the Departments of War, Army, and Air Force, members of Congress and their staff, as well as Governors and The Adjutants General in the Several States. The incumbent is responsible for the organizational vision and all functions of the NGB-IG including planning, formulation, and execution of policies, objectives, and goals. NGB-IG provides senior-level policy and analytical support to the CNGB and Vice CNGB, and Inspector General support to the Directors of the Army and Air National Guard and the NGB Director of Staff. As the functional manager for National Guard Inspector General activities, NGB-IG develops, leads, and implements the organizational vision of the National Guard Inspector General enterprise, incorporating high performance organization concepts to transform individual efforts into highly productive work-teams by integrating leadership, management, technical and team skills, values, and behaviors. The incumbent directs a required permanent staff of 38 military and civilian inspectors general and oversees the work of 54 State Inspectors General (O-6/O-5 military officers), and through them, up to 500+ inspectors general in the Several States. As the key executive for NGB-IG, the incumbent ensures National Guard equities are included in Department of War and the Departments of the Air Force and Army Inspector General programs and policies. NGB-IG serves as a member of the Defense Council on Integrity and Efficiency and represents National Guard equities at the Department of War Whistleblower Reprisal roundtable and other Departmental working groups. The incumbent is responsible for the execution of Department of War Inspector General programs and activities within the National Guard Bureau, and oversight and execution of the Army and Air Force Inspector General functions for the National Guard, including Army Inspections, Investigations, Assistance, Teach and Train, and Air Force Complaints Resolution and Inspections. This includes oversight of inspections, readiness assessments, sensitive matters, and Department of War, Army and Air Force Senior Official Investigation notifications to the Governors and the CNGB. On behalf of CNGB, NGB-IG also oversees intelligence and intelligence-related oversight responsibilities including the conduct of intelligence oversight inspections throughout the National Guard-assessing the compliance of all activities, operations, and programs with applicable laws, executive orders, policies, and directives. Additionally, NGB-IG is the conduit from the National Guard to the Department of War for reports of Questionable Intelligence Activities and Sensitive/ Highly Sensitive Matters.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The Director is responsible for the comprehensive development and execution of the Department of the Air Force (DAF) Enterprise Modeling & Simulation (M&S) strategy. The incumbent will review and update the M&S strategy for an enterprise-wide ecosystem while overseeing policy, defining key roles, and managing DAF participation in M&S forums and publications. The Director will develop and manage policy to create a formal M&S Certification process. This duty ensures that M&S-related systems, devices, and programs are compliant with established policies and that development efforts leverage existing products and standards. This is a critical mechanism for enforcing best practices and architectural principles in collaboration with the DAF M&S Steering Committee. The Director monitors, analyzes, and manages current and planned M&S investments across the DAF to identify opportunities for increased capability, return-on-investment, and mission effectiveness. The Director will assess M&S lifecycle costs and value, while also monitoring global M&S technology trends and best practices within the DoW to inform + SecAF about Modeling and Simulation Investments.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal Government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume. Your Resume must be 2 pages. If you submit a resume that exceeds the two-page limit, you will immediately be deemed ineligible for this position and will receive no further consideration. We recommend using a sans-serif font such as Lato, if available. Other acceptable options include Calibri, Helvetica, Arial, Verdana, Open Sans, Source Sans Pro, Roboto, or Noto Sans. Please use 0.5-inch margins. For formatting, consider using a 14-point font for titles and a 10-point font for the main body text. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a separate narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualification (TQ). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATION (TQ): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the following technical qualification. TQ: Demonstrated executive-level legal experience and expert legal leadership in advising senior-level officials on civil works regulatory programs, environmental law, and natural resources management. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQ, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants. The Department of the Army is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
MajorDuties: As the Deputy General Counsel (Civil Works), acts for, assists, and serves in discharging all the responsibilities of the General Counsel, Principal Deputy General Counsel, and the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works pertaining to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and civil works program which includes navigation, flood and storm damage reduction projects, Clean Water Act regulatory program; the acquisition, management, and disposal of civil works lands and national resources; and the overall protection of the environment. Advises the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works), and the Deputy Assistant Secretaries of the Army for Civil Works and their staffs on issues of national and international significance concerning the use and development of the nation's navigable waters, management of civil works lands and other resources, and the overall compliance with environmental laws. Issues regularly involve relations between the Army and other federal agencies, state and local government, as well as private citizens. Renders advice concerning the relationship between the executive and legislative branches, and other intra-governmental matters arising from the Army's dealing with other federal and state agencies. Participates in the formulation of policy concerning Army civil works programs; drafts and interprets legislation and identifies legal problems. Performs legal reviews of documents and extensive research into legislative histories and relevant case law; and prepares legal opinions providing answers, solutions and advice concerning civil works, national resources, real property, and related environmental matters. Provides support to the General Counsel, the Principal Deputy General Counsel, and the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works in the presentation of Army positions before Congress, Office of Management and Budget, Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Justice, other federal agencies, and in negotiations on civil works, national resources, and environmental issues with state and local government agencies. Serves under the general direction of the Senior Deputy General Counsel for Installations, Environment, and Civil Works. Guidance is received in terms of broad plans, policies, and programs of the Department of the Army. Supervises Office of the General Counsel attorneys supporting the civil works mission.

The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel of the DoW; Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation; Inspector General of the DoW; Director of Operational Test and Evaluation; Chief Information Officer of the DoW; Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs; Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer; and the Director of Administration and Management.

Major duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Directs the DoW Enterprise Architecture (EA) framework to ensure alignment with agency mission objectives and federal mandates. Establishes and directs DoW CIO Architectural Roadmaps. Leads the transition from legacy systems to a modernized, resilient, and interoperable IT ecosystem. Directs the identification, rapid prototyping, and scaling of emerging technologies (e.g., AI, 5G, Quantum, Advanced Data Analytics) to maintain technological superiority in coordination with DOW Research & Engineering. Establishes and implements an "innovation pipeline" to transition pilot programs into enterprise-level capabilities. Cultivates strategic partnerships with industry, academia, and federal research entities to forecast technology trends and operationalize them for the warfighter. Represents the DoW CIO in high-level architecture, engineering, and standards forums within the DoW, the Intelligence Community, the White House, and interagency and international forums.

Details.JobSummary: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is a Defense Agency of the Department of War (DoW) under the direction, authority, and control of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence & Security (USW (I&S)).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. To learn more about DCSA's mission and vision, visit: https://www.dcsa.mil/About-Us/Careers/.
MajorDuties: The Director of Financial Management and Comptroller serves as DCSA's senior financial-management executive and principal financial adviser to the DCSA Director and senior leadership. The incumbent directs and oversees the Agency's end-to-end financial-management program, including budget formulation and execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, internal controls, audit remediation, cost management, financial systems, and Working Capital Fund operations. The position provides independent, objective financial advice concerning Agency strategy, resource allocation, mission affordability, and financial risk. This is a Defense Intelligence Senior Executive Service Tier 2 position. The incumbent exercises executive direction and oversight of an annual financial portfolio of approximately $3.0 billion, comprising approximately $1.9 billion in Defense Working Capital Fund activity and $1.1 billion in appropriated funding. The incumbent directs the formulation, justification, execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, and performance assessment of these resources and oversees Working Capital Fund rate development, cost recovery, revenue and expense forecasting, cash management, customer billing, and long-term financial sustainability. Exercise executive direction and oversight of an annual financial portfolio exceeding $3.0 billion, comprising approximately $1.9 billion in Defense Working Capital Fund activity and $1.1 billion in appropriated funding. Direct the formulation, justification, execution, accounting, funds control, financial reporting, and performance assessment of these resources. Direct the financial governance of DCSA Working Capital Fund operations, including rate and price development, full-cost recovery, cash and corpus management, revenue, cost, and workload forecasting, customer billing, cost transparency, and the long-term financial sustainability of DCSA's fee-for-service operations. Establish and oversee DCSA's enterprise cost-accounting and cost-management framework. Ensure the consistent identification, accumulation, allocation, and reporting of direct and indirect costs to support Working Capital Fund rates, reimbursable pricing, program and activity cost transparency, customer billing, managerial decision-making, auditability, and assessment of mission efficiency. Serve as the principal financial adviser to the DCSA Director and senior leadership on financial management, resource allocation, fiscal risk, affordability, and the financial implications of Agency strategy and operating decisions. Represent DCSA before Departmental oversight organizations, the Office of Management and Budget, congressional committees and staff, Intelligence Community partners, customers, and other federal organizations on budgetary and financial-management matters. Establish and maintain an effective internal-control environment; direct financial-statement audit support, audit remediation, improper-payment and fraud-risk activities, and corrective actions addressing material weaknesses and other financial-management deficiencies. Provide executive oversight of financial management systems, business processes, financial data governance, and system modernization, ensuring reliable, timely, and decision-useful financial and cost information. Lead and develop DCSA's financial-management workforce and establish functional standards, workforce-development priorities, succession plans, and accountability for financial-management performance across headquarters and field organizations. Ensure compliance with appropriations law, fiscal controls, funds-control requirements, applicable accounting standards, and Departmental and Intelligence Community financial-management policies. Establish policy, governance, and financial controls for DCSA reimbursable activities and agreements. Oversee the development, review, acceptance, execution, billing, collection, reconciliation, closeout, and financial reporting of reimbursable orders to ensure full-cost recovery, proper use of funds, accurate customer billing, and compliance with applicable fiscal and financial-management requirements. Provide executive financial oversight of interagency agreements and other intra-governmental transactions, including agreements under the Economy Act and other applicable statutory authorities. Ensure that agreements contain appropriate funding authority, bona fide-need and period-of-availability determinations, cost estimates, billing provisions, internal controls, reconciliations, and closeout requirements.

Details.JobSummary: Deputy Director for Mission, Advanced Analytics PEO
MajorDuties: ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The Mission Deputy, PEO Advanced Analytics (PEO AA) coordinates, defines and advocates for solutions to the warfighter and analyst technology needs across NGA and the NSG. This position works across Maven, Enterprise GIS, and Analytic Technologies Program Offices to synchronize and maximize efficiency in meeting requirements in both mission spaces, and identifies opportunities to leverage mutually reinforcing investments. Ensures program directors are engaged with and responsive to customer needs and represents the voice of the customer in the creation of product road maps. The Mission Deputy, PEO AA participates in governance and oversight boards established by mission owners and represents PEO AA in NSG acquisition and technology strategies, and aligns those efforts to the NGA strategy and goals. Oversees the PEO framework for prioritizing and managing the transition of pilots, prototypes or other technology demonstrations; makes recommendations on integrating pilots into program baselines. Serves as the overall Analytic Workflow Modernization (AWM) lead for Analysis and NGA, representing the Agency investment in CIP/COP, and AWM related activities for DIE and ODNI interagency working groups and in the PPBE process. Provides guidance to Analysis, mission management and agency leadership on the implementation of AWM and CIP/COP. Engages with Analysis Leadership, working analysts and external users at the CCMD and Services to understand their technology needs, as well as help them understand available capabilities. Communicates PEO strategy, approach and mission value to oversight. Works closely with the PEO AA Director in co-leading three large software-centric major system acquisition, focused on all aspects of the analytic workflow, from orchestration and exploitation to computer vision, GIS and modeling. Supervises front office activities via the Chief of Staff to ensure PEO is fully engaged across the Agency, consistent in external messaging and cognizant of security risks to programmatic investments from the activities of foreign adversaries.
